chrome.build: On your computer, in the project folder, run pnpm extension:build. It creates apps/extension/dist.
chrome.load: In {chrome}, open chrome://extensions, turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked and choose the apps/extension/dist folder.
chrome.connect: Open the extension’s Options, check that the server URL is {url}, click Connect and approve in the window that opens. Or paste an access token from Settings.
chrome.use: Save a page with the toolbar button or Alt+Shift+S (on a {mac}, Option+Shift+S). Right-click a link and choose Save link to {app} to save just the link. The badge shows ✓ when it worked and ! when it didn’t.

shortcut.intro: You build two Shortcuts by hand, once; they then sync to your {iphone}, {ipad} and {mac} through {icloud}. The first sends the whole page from {safari}, so paywalled articles you can read are saved in full. The second, for other apps such as {chrome} on {iphone}, sends only the link.

before.heading: Before you start
before.scriptsOnIos: {iphone} and {ipad}: Settings → Apps → Shortcuts → Advanced → turn on Allow Running Scripts (on {ios} 17 and earlier: Settings → Shortcuts → Advanced).
before.scriptsOnMac: {mac}: in the Shortcuts app, Shortcuts → Settings → Advanced → turn on Allow Running Scripts. If {safari} still refuses to run the script, open {safari} → Settings → Advanced → turn on Show features for web developers, then in {safari}’s new Developer settings tab turn on Allow JavaScript from Apple Events, and restart {safari}.
before.token: Create an access token for this device in <tokens>Settings</tokens> and keep it at hand.

page.name: Save to {app}
page.heading: Shortcut 1: “{name}” ({safari})
page.create: In the Shortcuts app, tap + to make a new shortcut and name it “{name}”.
page.shareSheet: Open the shortcut’s details (the ⓘ button, or the name menu → Details) and turn on Show in Share Sheet. In the “Receive … from Share Sheet” line at the top, tap the input types and leave only Safari web pages selected.
page.script: Add the action Run JavaScript on Web Page (on a {mac}: Run JavaScript on Active Safari Tab). On {iphone} and {ipad} it uses the Shortcut Input as the page. Replace its script with this:
page.request: Add Get Contents of URL. Set the URL to {url}, then tap Show More:
page.headers: Headers: add Authorization with the value Bearer followed by your token, and Content-Type with the value application/json
page.body: Request Body: File, and choose the JavaScript Result variable
page.message: Add Get Dictionary Value: get the value for the key message in Contents of URL.
page.notification: Add Show Notification and put the Dictionary Value in it. It will say “{saved}”.
page.tryIt: Try it: in {safari}, open an article, tap Share and choose the shortcut. The first time, allow it to run JavaScript on the site (choose Always Allow).

link.name: Save link to {app}
link.heading: Shortcut 2: “{name}” (other apps)
link.create: Make a new shortcut, turn on Show in Share Sheet, and leave only URLs and Text as input types.
link.input: Add Get URLs from Input (from the Shortcut Input), then Get Item from List (First Item).
link.request: Add Get Contents of URL with the URL {url}. Under Show More: Method POST; header Authorization = Bearer + your token; Request Body JSON with two Text fields: url set to the Item from List variable, and source set to shortcut.
link.notification: Add Get Dictionary Value for message and Show Notification, as in Shortcut 1.
link.note: Links saved this way are downloaded by the server. Pages behind a login or paywall then show as “{previewOnly}”; open them in {safari} and use Shortcut 1 to keep the full copy.

android.open: Open this site in {chrome} on the phone and sign in.
android.install: Open {chrome}’s ⋮ menu and choose Add to Home screen → Install (or Install app).
android.share: In any app, tap Share and choose {app}. The link is saved and the Inbox opens.
